name: session-mutation-coordinator
body:
Session-scoped mutation coordinator — a MANDATORY deliverable and the project's chosen single-writer, not a contingent option. It is NOT a persistent daemon: `apg session start` launches a process for the duration of an update session; writes are routed to it; `apg session end` releases the DB/socket and exits (there is no accumulated buffer — each mutation was applied write-through).

The honest fix ladder (evaluate-fix-ladder) establishes that DB decoupling (option c) alone cannot meet serial-equivalence — the node-file read-modify-write (`edge_add`, src/node_cmd.rs:207) and the per-mutation git index commit (`git::commit_files`, src/git.rs:587-645) still race. A single writer over the WHOLE durable sequence is required. The coordinator is that single writer: it owns the worktree DB exclusively (single writer, so the lbug race is structurally gone) AND performs the node-file RMW + commit + projection record itself (coordinator-single-writer), so the races are serialized while a session is live. On top of that it amortizes the DB open/parse across N mutations (one open/parse serves the session) and applies each mutation's exact projection delta synchronously through the write-through projection — no batched flush, ever — which is its independent justification.

Status is unambiguous: the coordinator and its five child requirements below are MANDATORY — a plan for this project must realize them and the verify/coverage gate treats their solution nodes as in-scope; they are not left to a plan choice. The transparent direct path is separately serialized by the extended flock (evaluate-fix-ladder option a) so bursts are also safe without a live session.
